statements: Alex reports that an unnamed U.S. defense contractor shortlisted two remote technical candidates who appeared to be the same person on video while using different names and employment claims. Shared face and background, changed clothing, thin digital footprints, and location mismatch exposed the parallel identities.
Apply multiple times to one organization under separate identities
Reuse the same interview environment while changing clothing and biographical claims
Maintain thin or newly established digital footprints
Present location data inconsistent with the claimed identity
limitations: Alex labels the actor North Korean but does not publish government attribution or enough evidence to identify a person. The unnamed customer should remain generic despite its self-described sector.

statements: Correlate duplicate applicants across the same pipeline using privacy-respecting identity-continuity review
Compare repeated interview environment and identity signals only with authorized access and human review
Evaluate location, email, phone, and profile signals together rather than as automatic rejection rules
limitations: Signals require lawful, proportionate, accessible, privacy-preserving human review. Accent, ethnicity, nationality, visual similarity, camera behavior, geography, VPN use, remote work, or one device/network attribute must never act as a standalone detector.
